transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess I'm here because of work. The warehouse. The routing system there... it's, uh, it's not just a computer anymore. I've noticed things. It's been marking my moves. Sending these... messages through the scanners. I know they're trying to push me out because I'm one of the older guys there. That's... that's why I'm here.
Alongside these experiences at work, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand unusually energetic, irritable, or elated?

Energetic? No. Just... down, I guess. Empty. 

It's been like that for most of this whole trouble. Even when the warehouse stuff backs off for a bit and gets quiet, I still feel... I don't know. Just flat. I haven't been out fishing. My woodworking... I just leave the tools sitting. I don't even really sit down for family meals anymore. Just don't have it in me.
How long have you been noticing these messages and feeling that they're targeting you through the scanners—weeks, months, longer?
A long time. Uh... almost two years, I think. About a year and eight months since I started hearing them and... and realizing what the scanners were doing.
Over these past 20 months, have there been stretches of time when you were feeling like your normal self—not down or empty—but you still believed the scanners were sending you messages?

Yeah... I suppose there was a stretch. 

My mood had eased up a little bit. I was, uh, eating a little more... talking a bit more. But... even then, for several weeks, I still heard dispatch calling my number. I still knew the routing system was tracking me. 

So... yeah. It didn't stop.
Besides these messages from the scanners, have you noticed anything else unusual—like hearing voices when no one else is around, or finding it hard to organize your thoughts or speech?

I... yeah. I hear things. 

Not just at work. Even when I'm... when I'm just sitting in my garage. Everything's shut off, quiet. But I still hear them. Dispatch voices. Clear as day. Calling out my operator number. 

They... they say I'm dangerous. Or that security is coming to get me. 

As for my thoughts... I don't know. Just the voices.

Looking back over these past 20 months, would you say the down, empty mood has been present most of the time, or has it only come and gone in shorter periods compared to how long you've been hearing the voices and believing the scanners were tracking you?

Most of the time, yeah. 

Even... even when the stuff with the warehouse wasn't as loud in my head for a bit, I still felt... empty. Just down. Most of this whole twenty months, really. 

I haven't been able to... get back to things. Used to fish. Did some woodworking. Sat down for meals with the family. But... just couldn't. Most of the time.

During that stretch when your mood eased up, how many weeks did it last, and would you say you felt essentially back to your normal self—not just a little better—while still hearing the dispatch voices?

I... I don't know exactly how many weeks. Several, I guess. 

I wouldn't say I was completely normal. I just... my mood had eased some. I was eating a little more, talking a bit. But it didn't stop the rest of it. During those several weeks, I still heard dispatch calling my number. I still believed the routing system was tracking me. 

So... no, not completely back to normal. Just... eased some.
During those several weeks when your mood eased, were you completely free of feeling down or empty, or did you still feel some sadness or emptiness even though it was less intense?

I... I don't know if I was completely free of it. 

Like I said, the mood had just eased some. I was eating a little more. Talking a bit. But... I was still hearing dispatch. Still knew the routing system was on me. 

So... no, I guess the sadness didn't completely go away. Just... less heavy for those weeks.

latest_inference.note: Patient reports that even during the period of eased mood, sadness/emptiness never fully resolved, indicating no distinct 2+ week period of psychosis without significant depressive symptoms. This argues against F20.9 (schizophrenia) and clarifies the mood component as depressive rather than manic, narrowing F25.0 to the depressive subtype F25.1.
